questions.explanation: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor. It accepts electrons and protons to form water, and this final acceptance permits electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue normally. [ev_resp02_terminal_acceptor; ev_resp02_accepts_electrons; ev_resp02_forms_water; ev_resp02_flow_continues]

options.text: Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue.
Oxygen is the initial electron donor; it accepts electrons and protons to form water, allowing electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it releases electrons and protons to form water, allowing electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue.
Oxygen is the terminal electron acceptor; it accepts electrons and protons to produce peroxide, allowing electron flow through the aerobic electron transport chain to continue.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains oxygen’s role at the end of the aerobic electron transport chain?
